title: AI workflow automation for support teams: How to build skills | Pylon
summary: Learn how AI workflow automation helps support teams turn repeatable tasks into skills, improve resolution speed, and scale with guardrails and visibility.
body_markdown:
As support volume grows, so does the amount of repetitive daily tasks. Your team has to spend more time gathering account details, updating tickets, and coordinating fixes, often across systems that don’t share data. As a result, simple requests can take more time and effort than they should.


AI workflow automation gives[B2B support teams](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/b2b-customer-service-best-practices-strategies) a way to standardize routine processes. But before automating a workflow, you’ll need to understand which steps can be handled effectively by AI and where human judgment is still needed.


In this guide, we’ll talk about which support tasks are worth automating, and explain how to turn existing processes into repeatable AI skills. We’ll also preview what changes when AI automation tools become part of your team’s day-to-day operations.


## What’s AI workflow automation for support teams?


Triggers in Pylon


AI workflow automation uses artificial intelligence to complete tasks your team would otherwise have to do by hand. Automation isn’t a new[customer support tool](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-support-automation-tools) , but the addition of AI has made it more powerful and flexible.


Traditional automation tools follow pre-defined rules to perform specific actions. For example, a help desk could[automatically assign tickets](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-ticketing-systems) based on keywords in customer conversations, or copy customer data from a help query to a CRM system. This saves some time, but requests that don’t match the rules perfectly will still need manual input.


Automated[agentic AI](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/agentic-ai-use-cases) uses large language models to interpret unstructured data, like a support conversation that doesn’t follow an expected pattern.[AI agents](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-set-up-ai-agents) can use context to decide on next steps and recognize when a human team member needs to step in.


This opens up plenty of opportunities to automate repeat work throughout the support flow. Your team spends less time on manual steps, which means they can fix issues faster with fewer handoffs. Standardized workflows also help managers spot delays and find solutions.


## How to design reusable AI skills for workflow automation: 4 steps


B2B support teams have plenty of repeat processes worth[turning into AI skills](https://www.usepylon.com/ai-agents/skills) . A skill uses current knowledge and best practices to build a reusable set of instructions that both team members and AI agents can follow.


Let’s look at how you can do that in four steps.


### 1. Identify a workflow pattern


Start with a recurring support task that has a clear trigger and a set outcome. For instance, your team could follow the same process whenever a customer disputes a charge on their invoice. Review the docs you already have in place, and write down what the workflow looks like from end to end.


### 2. Define skill inputs


Next, decide what information a team member or AI agent needs in order to follow the process accurately. For a billing dispute, they could start by gathering customer context and[reviewing SLAs](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/sla-best-practices) .


You’ll also need to explain how that information should be reviewed and what the next steps should be. The skill could check to see if a disputed charge matches the customer’s subscription terms, before flagging a legitimate billing error and escalating the ticket.


### 3. Set triggers and actions


If you’re using Pylon’s agentic support platform, you can[build a custom skill](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/agents/skills) or ask[Assist Agent](https://www.usepylon.com/ai-agents/assist) to turn a successful resolution into a reusable AI workflow. Teams that already have skill files in other AI tools can import them into Pylon instead of recreating them.


Your skill should define which actions the AI can complete on its own, and which require human approval. It’s also important to create role-based permissions that control who can authorize sensitive actions, like issuing refunds or contacting customers directly. An AI agent could investigate a disputed charge and draft an explanation, but leave the refund decision and final email to an experienced team member.


With Pylon, you can configure[Automations](https://www.usepylon.com/ai-agents/automations) to run skills if specific events happen, like when a ticket about a certain topic enters the queue. The AI agent can start the investigation automatically and summarize its findings, then pass the case over to your team if it requires a decision or an approval.


### 4. Reuse and refine the skill


Before officially rolling out your new skill, test it against real support cases to see if it works as intended. Pylon’s Assist Agent can suggest improvements, which your team can then review and apply. Once you've tested a skill and know it’s effective, you can reuse it as a starting point for similar support processes.


## What a support workflow looks like with skill-based automation


AI fields in Pylon


Once a skill is up and running, AI agents can follow its instructions to move issues through the support flow. Depending on the use case, the AI could finish the work on its own or prepare information so a human team member can step in.


Here are a few examples of how you can[automate customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-support-automation-software) with Pylon:


- **Bug reports:** Automations investigate issues when defined triggers occur. They can check available logs and previous reports, then prepare that context for human review.
- **Subscription plan and billing questions:** Assist Agent uses account context to draft responses your team can edit and send.
- **How-to questions:** Support Agent answers customer questions autonomously using approved knowledge. If it can’t resolve the issue based on that context, the AI summarizes the issue and routes the conversation to your team.
- **Outage follow-ups:**[Pylon's Broadcasts](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/broadcasts/overview) can send status updates to all impacted accounts at once, so your team doesn't have to write and follow up on individual conversations.


### Skills in practice: An example


To see how skills work, let’s consider what could happen when a customer reports a software bug:


1. **Intake:** A new bug report enters the support queue and triggers AI workflow automation.
2. **Context retrieval:** Automations[track issues](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/issues-management-system) in the customer’s account context and search for similar tickets.
3. **Intent detection:** The AI agent classifies the customer issue, then decides if the problem matches a known bug or needs further investigation.
4. **Action:** The agent prepares a report that summarizes its findings and includes helpful context.
5. **Approval:** A support team member reviews the AI investigation and approves follow-up actions as needed.
6. **Reporting:** The skill records its activity, so your team can review what happened and spot opportunities for improvement.

## FAQ


### How does AI workflow automation differ from low-code and no-code platforms?


Low-code and no-code platforms let teams build automated workflows with little or no programming. These traditional automations follow predefined instructions, and they tend to be fairly simple and rigid.


AI workflow automation is more flexible, able to interpret problems and take steps toward resolving them. For example, a support team could create a low-code rule to[automatically escalate tickets](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/escalation-tools-customer-support) after 24 hours without a response. An automated AI workflow could go further to review relevant logs, classify the problem, and prepare a solution for approval.


### How does Pylon use AI workflow automation to help support teams?


Pylon’s[AI support tools](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-support-tools) let your team turn recurring processes into reusable skills. AI agents can investigate issues using customer context and connected systems, then help your team find solutions and draft responses.


### What governance and controls does Pylon provide for AI workflows?


Pylon uses[role-based access controls](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/platform/roles-and-user-management) to manage what users and agentic AI are able to access. Your team can set approval requirements for sensitive actions, and define when an AI workflow needs to route to a human team member. Plus, audit logs let admins review activity and track changes to workflow settings.


### How do support teams measure results from AI workflow automation?


Managers can measure AI workflow performance with[key support metrics](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-track-support-metrics) , like average handling time and the percentage of issues resolved with agentic AI. Choose a few KPIs based on your goals, and compare their histories before and after automating the workflow with AI.
